Harvey Weinstein wanted 45 minutes cut from Princess Mononoke. Studio Ghibli's producer answered with a katana and two words: no cuts. The film went out untouched, and Miyazaki later summed it up in three words: I defeated him. ⚔️

instagram_caption:
Studio Ghibli once gave Harvey Weinstein a samurai sword. ⚔️

In 1999 Miramax was handling the US release of Princess Mononoke, and Weinstein wanted it cut from 135 minutes down to 90. Ghibli had been burned before: an American distributor had once trimmed about twenty minutes from Nausicaa and renamed it Warriors of the Wind.

So producer Toshio Suzuki bought a katana, a blunt replica from a prop shop according to a colleague's memoir, presented it in a Miramax conference room and shouted: Mononoke Hime, no cut. For years the story was that Miyazaki had posted the sword himself. Asked in 2005, he laughed: 'Actually, my producer did that.' He said New York had bombarded him with demands for cuts, then added, smiling: 'I defeated him.'

The film opened uncut in America and made about two million dollars. Four years later Spirited Away won the Oscar, and Miyazaki stayed home. He later said he hadn't wanted to visit a country that was bombing Iraq.

Bonus: he 'retired' in 2013, came back, and won a second Oscar at 83. His producer says he now regrets telling the world he was done.

Sword or lawyers? 👇
